messages:
lee: Heads-up — ACME flagged missing audit export events after our maintenance window. They report ~20% of policy_change and role_grant events absent from the S3 export starting 2026-03-03 02:12 UTC. They see a lot of 403s in the forwarder logs around the same time.

maya: thanks lee. do we have the forwarder logs and the manifest path? any tenant id?

lee: tenant: acme-42. manifest path they shared: s3://redwood-audit-exports/tenants/acme-42/2026-03-03/manifest-20260303T0212.json. Forwarder snippet attached below (redacted):

lee: ```
2026-03-03T02:12:34Z forwarder audit-forwarder-1 ERROR PutObject failed tenant=acme-42 key=events/2026/03/03/chunk-00023.gz status=403 error=AccessDenied
2026-03-03T02:12:35Z forwarder audit-forwarder-1 WARN zero-byte manifest detected tenant=acme-42 manifest=manifest-20260303T0212.json
2026-03-03T02:12:36Z forwarder audit-forwarder-1 ERROR siem-forwarder tenant=acme-42 push failed status=403 response="{\"message\":\"Forbidden\"}"
```

sam: pinging in. Any recent credential or cert rotations for the accessor/forwarder? 403s + zero-byte manifests smell like permission failures during a key rotation or client cert mismatch.

maya: Security rotated accessor client certs during the 02:00 UTC maintenance per the rollout notes. KMS/HSM rekey also ran at 02:05 UTC for tenant acme-42 (scheduled). I suspect a short window where forwarders couldn't rewrap envelopes.

sam: confirm steps I want to run for triage: 1) check accessor service logs for TLS handshake failures and mTLS client CN mismatch; 2) check forwarder logs for envelope rewrap errors (KMS Decrypt/Encrypt fails); 3) inspect S3 PutObject IAM errors and bucket policy evaluation; 4) examine manifest entries to see which chunk ids are missing.

auditbot: automated-check: found 14 zero-byte manifests and 27 PutObject 403s for tenant=acme-42 between 2026-03-03T02:05 and 02:20Z. Marking as correlated with cert rotation window.

lee: customer says their SIEM got a gap and wants a replay/backfill plan. They also asked whether retention/ttl could have dropped events (they're within retention).

maya: initial ask to eng-security/oncall: can we confirm if the forwarder had stale KMS grants or if the accessor cert rotation briefly rejected forwarder connection? If it's a rewrap race, we need to run a re-encrypt replay for those shards and re-upload.

sam: quick repro command to validate accessor TLS acceptance:

sam: ```bash
# simulate forwarder push to accessor endpoint with current client cert
curl -v --cert client.pem --key client.key \
  -H "X-Tenant-ID: acme-42" \
  -F "file=@chunk-00023.gz" \
  https://audit-accessor.internal.redwood/v1/upload
```

sam: expected: 200 OK. If we get 403/401 or TLS handshake fail -> cert mapping problem. For KMS errors, check forwarder logs for: "KMS Decrypt failed: InvalidCiphertextException" or HSM logs for nonce/migrate errors.

maya: sam — can you own the security triage? eng-oncall, can you schedule a short incident and ping customer success for a repro window?

eng-oncall: oncall ack'd. will create incident INC-2026-ACME-AUDIT and add sam, maya, and storage-sre. will also pull the affected manifests and list the missing chunk ids. ETA 20m.

lee: customer is okay with a 1-hour replay window and wants confirmation when we start/finish.

sam: plan once triage confirms root cause: 1) rewrap affected envelope keys for tenant acme-42 (use rewrap tool with HSM policy), 2) reprocess and re-upload non-zero chunks, 3) update manifests and trigger SIEM forwarder re-send for the missing chunk list, 4) run validation query to ensure policy_change events count matches customer's count. I'll include checksums in the replay log.

maya: cc @storage-sre: if re-upload needed, please coordinate on S3 object lifecycle/overwrite semantics (we might see chunk id collisions). Also confirm we won't trigger duplicate ingestion in SIEM (we should mark replayed objects with replay=true metadata).

sam: noted. if the cause is client-cert CN mismatch, fix is: update accessor cert mapping and restart forwarder clients or push updated client certs. If cause is KMS grant expiration, grant new decrypt rights and run rewrap.

eng-oncall: incident created and linked to customer ticket. I'll post updates in this thread and in the incident channel.

lee: thanks — please keep me posted so I can update ACME. :pray:

maya: adding this to weekly postmortem if we confirm rotation window produced the gap. low-risk mitigation: make rewrap idempotent and add short retry/backoff in forwarder to avoid zero-byte manifests during maintenance windows.

sam: I'll upload initial triage findings to the incident within 30m.

eng-oncall: last note — manifest path for easy access: s3://redwood-audit-exports/tenants/acme-42/2026-03-03/manifest-20260303T0212.json. refer to INC-2026-ACME-AUDIT for artifacts.
